ARX / 6 · P6-A ENGINEERING REVIEW

Transparent covers.
Retained metal structure.

Prototype, not a manufacturing release. Thermal limits and exact-print qualification remain open. The renders are real geometry-based path tracing, not evidence of measured print transparency.

Native 4K/64-path proof, downsampled in linear light. The primary arm structure and joint heat spreaders remain metal.

This is an implemented cover-and-mount conversion of the refined P5 CAD, not a whole-plastic arm or a render-only transparency override. Ten removable covers become PETG; the load-carrying metal frames, six structural heat-spreader cases, bearings, reducers, motor/brake mounts, gripper force path and both spring-containment assemblies remain metal.

Delivered

The package contains a native STEP operating assembly, the ten print-local cover STEP/STL files, individual modified/new STEP parts, all CAD and rendering code, orthotropic solid-tetrahedron FEM code and outputs, fresh baseline/P6 contact simulations, thermal and fit sensitivity studies, a searchable HTML part-decision register and an eight-page engineering dossier. Two real path-traced stills are supplied. There is no new motion-film export or qualified physical teardown procedure.

Actual component conversion

Six rear service covers: IDs 3, 33, 67, 101, 133 and 169. Four link service panels: IDs 210, 215, 220 and 225. The service caps are 4 mm thick except J4 (101), which is 3.4 mm to avoid the forearm frame. The upper panels are 51 x 138 x 4 mm; the shorter panels are 51 x 32 x 4 mm. All 278 original IDs have an explicit keep/change decision in assets/part-conversion-map.json. Existing supplier components remain envelope models; no internal teeth/windings are invented.

Forty revised screws and 120 new mount pieces bring the model to 398 part instances. Each PETG cover uses four 5.6 mm clearance holes around 4 mm OD / 2.7 mm ID metal sleeve spacers. Retaining washers are 8 mm OD and 0.7 mm thick. Silicone seats are modeled at 0.3 mm installed thickness (0.5 mm nominal free thickness is a design assumption). Link-panel spacers include 2.2 mm metal seat risers; caps seat directly on their original mounting lands. Proposed screw lengths are 10 mm at caps and 12 mm at panels. Nominal metal engagement is 5.0 mm, 5.6 mm for J4 and 4.8 mm for panels. Actual thread depth, seating, gasket compression and retention must be checked; no tightening torque is released.

The tightening load path is screw -> retaining washer -> metal spacer -> existing metal land. PETG is retained by a compliant seat rather than being the direct bolt-preload member. This is a custom prototype arrangement, not a certified supplier compression-limiter joint. Heat-set inserts are deliberately not put in the PETG: the retained metal threads are used. [3]

Engineering results

CAD mass/inertia integration gives a net assembly mass change of +53.52 g, including enlarged panels and metal hardware. The new body COMs and full inertia tensors are in assets/p6-mass-properties.json. Lighter-density polymer does not automatically make this revised assembly lighter.

All 170 modified/new STEP parts reimport as valid single solids. The new covers and all 120 new mounting parts were screened against retained geometry at 17 recorded poses; 1653 candidate Boolean intersections were evaluated, with no unintended overlap above 0.05 mm3. This is a sampled nominal new-part screen, not continuous swept-volume, worst-tolerance, cable or full-robot collision certification. The two inherited reference spring instances remain multisolid source geometry and are not requalified.

The final mount sensitivity sweep passes all 90 assumed cases, including PETG CTE 60–100 micrometres/(m K), differential temperature rise 25–50 K, 0.20 mm combined hole-location allowance and the stated hole/spacer size allowances. Minimum remaining modeled radial clearance is 0.066 mm. The initial 4.8 mm holes failed 28/90 cases; those results are retained under reports/rejected-initial. Final hole size and location need a measurement/finishing operation; no as-printed dimensional guarantee is made.

Finite-element stiffness screen

Four representative covers were solved as 3D linear orthotropic solid-tetrahedron models, with actual outline/hole dimensions, an area-integrated 10 N load over a 12 mm top patch and self-weight normal to the cover. Washer-seat patches provide bilateral normal support; two small patches remove in-plane rigid motion. This omits nonlinear gasket contact, lift-off, thread compliance and print defects. Rim fillets are present in CAD but omitted from the extrusion submodels.

Assumed screening properties: E1=E2=1.5 GPa, E3=0.8 GPa; G12=0.54 GPa, G13=G23=0.28 GPa; nu12=0.35, nu13=nu23=0.28; density 1250 kg/m3. Selected screening stress thresholds are 12 MPa in-plane, 5 MPa through thickness and 4 MPa shear. These are not material certifications. They are deliberately distinct from the suppliers' typical coupon results. [1,2]

At the finest executed 1.25 mm mesh, predicted maximum deflections are: large cap 0.035 mm, thin J4 cap 0.026 mm, long panel 0.256 mm and short panel 0.015 mm. Last-step deflection changes are approximately 8–10%; these are screening estimates, not mesh-independent precision results. Peak stress near imposed supports is mesh-sensitive. Linear 50 N extrapolation exceeds the assumed peak threshold for some covers and is explicitly retained as a failed handling screen, not an impact or fracture simulation. Cover-only eigenmodes are included at the 2.5 mm mesh; whole-robot flexible modes were not solved.

Fresh contact dynamics

Both the refined-metal baseline and P6 were run for 10 seconds at 1/2400 second integration steps in the bundled MuJoCo WASM model. The independent puck is handled by contact/friction, not a visual weld. The inherited gripper controller initially overshot to 43.86 mm against the CAD upper travel of 38.5 mm. Increasing the reconstructed controller's velocity damping from 12 to 120 N s/m removed that overrun; no position clamping or CAD limit widening was used. The same revised controller is applied to both comparison runs.

P6 jaw coordinates remain 18.964–38.000 mm. The modeled placements are 0.139 mm at B and 0.134 mm on return to A. Peak shoulder command is 9.686 N m, changing by 0.096 N m from the matched baseline. These are this reconstruction's numerical results, not measured robot accuracy or proof of motor ratings.

This is not the original 28-scenario electromechanical validation. The model has rigid-body masses, averaged control commands and simplified contact proxies. It does not solve the cover FEM together with the controller, a full self-collision model, motor thermal/electrical limits, FOC, structural fatigue or functional safety. The controller source is a simulation model, not released hardware firmware.

Thermal and creep limits

A two-node transient cover-temperature model tests 40 assumed combinations of ambient temperature, imposed metal-case temperature and mount conductance. It includes through-wall conduction, convection and radiation but does not predict motor winding heat. 25/40 cases exceed the chosen 55 C screening ceiling. For example, a large cap at 25 C ambient beside an 85 C metal case reaches approximately 58–67 C, depending on assumed mount conductance. The clear covers are therefore conditional prototypes: heat-soak testing or a metal-cover fallback is necessary. The 55 C ceiling is a project choice, not a continuous-use rating inferred from HDT or glass transition. [1,2]

The creep study is a compliance-factor sensitivity sweep (1x, 2x, 4x, 8x), not a timed viscoelastic lifetime prediction. The long-panel 10 N deflection becomes 1.026 mm under the 4x compliance assumption. No unmeasured creep constants, service hours, permanent deformation or fatigue life are claimed.

Transparent render implementation

The renderer now traces solid PETG entry/exit boundaries with Fresnel reflection, Snell refraction, total internal reflection, thickness-dependent RGB absorption and stochastic volume scattering. It is not alpha transparency. Appearance assumptions: IOR 1.57, absorption (3, 1.4, 0.65) per metre, scattering 28 per metre, HG g=0.78, restrained 0.20 mm layer/0.44 mm road microtexture. These are not optical measurements of a printed specimen. Bulk/resin data does not establish the clarity of a particular printed wall. [4,5]

Both proofs are native 3840 x 2160, 64 camera paths per native pixel, up to 14 surface/scattering events. Three geometry-guided denoising stages precede linear-light Lanczos downsampling to 1080p. The code retains anisotropic metal materials, area lights, glossy indirect light and actual geometry. No image generation or mesh substitution is used. Refraction/volume caustics may remain noisy; the renderer does not include volumetric next-event sampling or overlapping dielectric-medium stacks. No perfect photorealism or real-print clarity is asserted.

Required release gates

Qualify the exact clear filament, printer, orientation, drying and print profile using XY/Z coupons, stiffness and retained-load tests. Confirm dimensional finishing of every mount hole and its position, minimum edge ligaments, metal thread engagement, sleeve seating and positive cover retention. Test the assembled gasket/mount for vibration, thermal cycling and pull-through. Heat-soak each converted cap on the real drive at the intended duty cycle; keep the metal cap where the allowable thermal envelope is not met. Assess creep, UV/chemical exposure and repeated cover servicing. Neither clear caps nor this study are a fragment-containment, ingress-protection, EMC, fire or functional-safety qualification.

Suggested print-local STL orientation is flat with the cover build axis normal to its broad face. A 0.20 mm layer and solid construction are prototype study assumptions, not a released print recipe. No G-code is provided. Primary frames, bearing fits, brake supports and spring-energy containment are not converted to PETG.

Reproduce

Python packages are pinned in requirements.txt; native tools additionally require a C++17 OpenMP compiler and Node.js. The original refined CAD input BREP files, geometry binary and mass records are included under inputs/refined and assets, so the build does not require an inaccessible prior workspace.

python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python source/build_p6.py
python source/update_dynamics.py
node source/capture.mjs p5refined
node source/capture.mjs p6
python source/audit_geometry.py
python source/screen_covers.py
python source/refine_fea.py
python source/engineering_screen.py
python source/export_p6_native.py
g++ -O3 -march=native -fopenmp -std=c++17 source/pathtrace.cpp -o source/pathtrace
g++ -O2 -fopenmp -std=c++17 source/test_optics.cpp -o source/test_optics
source/test_optics
python source/render_petg_proofs.py
python source/build_documents.py
python source/verify_package.py

The archive includes no font files. The MuJoCo license and third-party notices are retained. Final hashes and the executed verification scope are in the delivery verification JSON.

References

[1] PolyLite PETG technical data sheet. https://wiki.polymaker.com/polymaker-products/more-about-our-products/documents/technical-data-sheets/petg-pet/polylite-tm-petg
Primary reference: density 1.25 g/cm3; typical XY/Z modulus 2116.8/1898.7 MPa and tensile strength 50.8/42.8 MPa. These are that supplier's test results, not this print's allowables.

[2] Ultimaker PETG TDS v1.00. https://um-support-files.ultimaker.com/materials/2.85mm/tds/PETG/Ultimaker-PETG-TDS-v1.00.pdf
Different print-system reference: typical Z modulus 1711 MPa and Z tensile break strength 19.0 MPa. It illustrates why one generic printed-PETG strength is not defensible.

[3] SPIROL compression limiters. https://www.spirol.com/product/compression-limiters/
Reference for carrying fastener tightening loads through metal rather than crushing plastic. The P6 custom floating sleeve/seat is not a selected or rated SPIROL assembly.

[4] PBRT, fourth edition: Dielectric BSDF. https://pbr-book.org/4ed/Reflection_Models/Dielectric_BSDF
Reference for Fresnel reflection, refraction and radiance transport conventions. P6 uses its own native renderer, not PBRT.

[5] Eastman Spectar Renew 14471-50 copolyester data. https://productcatalog.eastman.com/tds/ProdDatasheet.aspx?pn=eastman+spectar+renew+14471-50+copolyester+&product=71123771
A resin-family reference for nD about 1.57, not an optical measurement of the proposed printed covers. The render treats 1.57 as an assumed appearance parameter.
